review_notes: I read the whole file. It has two theorems: the helper `tsum_integral_eq_sum_integral_comp_add_of_forall_not_mem_range` and the large `solution` statement. Neither theorem is tagged `@[simp]`, and the file does not define or tag any simp lemmas, so there is no simp set of its own to assess for orientation, cycles or competing rules. All the `simp` calls in the proofs are `simp only` with explicit lemma lists, for example `simp only [hoff e hne', map_zero, mul_zero, Finset.sum_const_zero, integral_zero]`. These do not depend on or alter any global simp normal form. The long `attribute [-simp]` and `attribute [-instance]` lines only switch off simp lemmas and instances from other files in the project. They do not add or reorder anything in this file's own simp interface. I did not follow those lines into their sources. The vanishing-off-range computation appears three times as an ad hoc `simp only` (in `hint`, `hsum` and `key`). That is repetition inside proofs, and I did not count it as a simp-interface defect. I found no justified finding under this rubric. I did not open the imported definition files, so I cannot rule out problems in how they set up simp. Those would lie outside this file.
